text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.

- Thousands of employees and ex-employees at mobile phone plants have the know-how to forge security codes of digital Global System of Mobile Telecommunication (GSM) handsets, needed if you plan to sell stolen or illegal handsets.
- Insurer Sampo has introduced car insurance pricing based on the owner as well as the car. Age and area of residence to affect premiums. @
- Helsinki air defence unit gets new Russian MUK M1 missile system, paying only 150 million markka for the one billion markka system with the rest cleared against Russia's debts.
- Pipe and furniture maker Asko plans to invest much in its fast-growing plastic pipes unit Uponor which may in three-four years be as big as the group is today, CEO says.
- Finland's Office for Free Competition will get a massive workload if a government plan to let it monitor mergers and acquisitions materialises. @
- Helsinki telephone operator HPY starts planning a share issue, says its projected market capitalisation in case of a listing would place its on the bourse's main list.
- Finnish coffee roaster Paulig to end coffee roasting in Wimbledon to start exporting coffee for the UK market from Finland instead.
- Finns with business degrees best paid in finance; public sector pay the worst, survey shows. @
- Salmonella bacteria found in 17 tonnes of imported French turkey which will be returned to the seller. The lot had been isolated and none of it sold or processed.
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen sent an unusual letter to all ministries to point out that they must offer services also in Swedish, Finland's second national language.
- Lipponen now says it is uncertain when unemployment can be halved from where it was two years ago. The earlier target has been to halve it by 1999. @
